title: Quantify the near-trial BIT margin needed with the 451-factor transfer
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

For the #7863 451-factor loss budgets and retained seven-stage transfer/claim selector, a claim strictly above 0.003879929046155 needs a raw BIT trial strictly above 0.0038799290488400000004497. The unchanged BIT invoice has a directed deficit, and the unchanged rational invoice remains positive at the corresponding tested rate. The separate conditional stock-depth result assumes a fixed-prime finite product ledger; physical stock is still an obligation.

## Task and overlap

Uses #7863 at b3e4412fe01f07dc58305616fabf96345f49a781 and #7830 at 87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15. #7868 at 3f7c3c1f2a9a0963736562037e01fe41aec46b8c uses a distinct streamed ternary and periodic stock construction at the original κ. This packet prices the retained 451 selector and a named higher target.

## Validation and credit

The clean standard-library replay and self-test independently reprice both sides with directed arithmetic and authenticate copied members against the exact #7863 archive. The expected receipt, source input, bad archive and optimized-execution controls were rejected. OpenAI Codex assisted. Source contributors are credited in NOTICE and the frozen pins.

## Open next questions

A positive changed BIT word must rebind both consumers, recheck changed moments, and prove the prime, owned erasure, physical stock, precision and outer obligations. This packet claims no new κ.
